title: Cherry Crumb Pie (Frozen Cherries)
source: America's Test Kitchen (filling), Smitten Kitchen (crumb), Stella Parks (crust), adapted

items.body: Make one shell on the Flaky Pie Dough card: rolled, chilled at least 2 h and blind-baked. It can be baked up to 12 h ahead.
Weigh the frozen cherries into a metal bowl and thaw at room temp until soft all the way through, ≈2 h.
While the cherries thaw, whisk the brown sugar and granulated sugar into the melted butter in a bowl until smooth.
Stir the flour and salt into the butter mixture until no dry flour shows. Press it into the bowl and cool until firm, 10–15 min.
Break it into ½–¾ in chunks, leaving some smaller. Bigger chunks stay soft in the middle. Spread on a plate or quarter sheet pan and refrigerate at least 30 min.
Tip the thawed cherries into the strainer set over a bowl. Press gently until 240 g (1 cup) of juice has collected. Leave the cherries in the strainer.

Whisk the cornstarch into 30 g (2 tbsp) of the cold juice. Bring the rest of the juice to a boil in the saucepan. Whisk in the cornstarch mix and the lemon juice and boil, whisking, until thick and glossy, ≈1 min. Off the heat, stir in the almond extract.
In a large bowl, whisk the sugar, cornstarch and salt. Add the drained cherries and toss to coat, then fold in the thickened juice from the saucepan.
Rack in the lower-middle, oven to 350 °F (177 °C). Set the cooled shell on the half sheet pan. Scrape in all the filling and spread it level.
Scatter all the cold crumb chunks over the filling without pressing them in. Leave a few small gaps so you can see the juice. Cover the crust rim with strips of foil so it doesn’t burn.

Bake until the crumb is deep golden, juice bubbles thickly in the gaps at the center (not only at the edge), and a probe pushed through the crumb into the middle reads at least 203 °F (95 °C), ≈1–1¼ h. Crumb browning too fast? Lay foil loosely on top.
Cool on a rack at least 4 h so the filling sets before slicing.

nutritionSource: USDA FoodData Central: Branded Foods labels (Meijer red tart cherries, frozen, 12 oz, FDC 2638814; King Arthur All-Purpose; Morton; almond extract counted as Morton Bassett) and SR Legacy (sugar, brown sugar, unsalted butter, cornstarch, lemon juice). Shell from its card.
notes: Filling from America’s Test Kitchen’s Tart Cherry Crumb Pie, with ¼ tsp Morton in place of its ½ tsp table salt. Crumb from the Dutch Apple Crumb Pie card. The prebaked shell and this bake time are new, so go by the bubbling and the probe.
Check that the bag says pitted. If it doesn’t, pit the cherries after they thaw. The last ⅓ bag is ≈113 g.
Keeps 2 days at room temp, loosely covered; the fridge softens the crumb. To recrisp, 300 °F (149 °C) for 15–20 min, not the microwave.
